scenario.name: Red Hat Security, CNCF Tetragon & MITRE — Container CAP_SYS_MODULE Host Kernel Module (finit_module) Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a skyscraper where every sealed tenant suite rides on the exact same central elevator engine in the basement. Discovering that their suite badge accidentally includes elevator-mechanic clearance, a tenant builds a homemade gear that fits the exact engine model, bolts it straight into the central basement machinery from inside their room, and trips a permanent red warning lamp on the skyscraper master engineering console. In this scenario (T1082, Red Hat Security, CNCF Tetragon & MITRE, Container CAP_SYS_MODULE Host Kernel Module , finit_module Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16, then invoking finit_module / init_module, then host Kernel /proc/modules Taint Flag. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16, then Invoking finit_module / init_module, then Host Kernel /proc/modules Taint Flag, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1082 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16 (CAP_SYS_MODULE) & Host uname -r
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1082 - System Information Discovery)
stages.description: Inside the sealed tenant suite, the intruder checks their badge stamp list and the central elevator nameplate, discovering both that they hold rare engine-room installation rights and the exact make and model of the shared basement engine. Because all containers on a Linux node share the same host kernel, a container process checks /proc/self/status for CapEff bit 16 (0x0000000000010000 = CAP_SYS_MODULE) and runs uname -r to match the host kernel ABI version (logged in Linux Audit Event 63 with DetectedCapability=CAP_SYS_MODULE , Bit 16, PodIdentity=default/legacy-net-agent, SensorSource=Cilium Tetragon eBPF so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes capsh --decode=00000000a80525fb (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , capsh --decode=00000000a80525fb configuring pod security contexts, volume mounts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1082 during "Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16 , CAP_SYS_MODULE & Host uname -r" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact uname -r && cat /proc/version runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , uname -r && cat /proc/version via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact ar so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1082 during "Inspecting /proc/self/status CapEff Bit 16 , CAP_SYS_MODULE & Host uname -r" , Because all containers on a Linux node share the same host kernel, a container process checks /proc/self/status for CapEff bit 16 , 0x0000000000010000 = CAP_SYS_MODULE and runs uname -r to match the host kernel ABI version while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Invoking finit_module (Syscall 313) / init_module (Syscall 175) via insmod
stages.subtitle: Escape to Host & Persistence (T1547.006 - Kernel Modules and Extensions)
stages.description: Fashioning a custom metal gear tailored to that exact engine model, the intruder feeds it through the basement installation slot straight into the spinning central elevator core, immediately bypassing every wall separating the suite from the rest of the building. The container process executes insmod /tmp/net_diag.ko, which invokes sys_finit_module (syscall 313) or sys_init_module (syscall 175) to load the ELF relocatable kernel object directly into host Ring-0 kernel memory (logged in Linux Audit Event 313 with Syscall=sys_finit_module , 313, LoadedModulePath=/tmp/net_diag.ko , Container OverlayFS, AuditRuleKey=kernel_module_load so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ausearch -sc init_module,finit_module,delete_module -i (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -sc init_module,finit_module,delete_module -i via System / Runtime Execution Interf so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1547.006 during "Invoking finit_module , Syscall 313 / init_module , Syscall 175 via insmod" , The container process executes insmod /tmp/net_diag.ko, which invokes sys_finit_module , syscall 313 or sys_init_module , syscall 175 to load the ELF relocatable kernel object directly into host Ring-0 kernel memory while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact dmesg -T | grep -E "taints kernel|module verification" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , dmesg -T | grep -E "taints kernel|module verification" via System / Runtime Execution Interf so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1547.006 during "Invoking finit_module , Syscall 313 / init_module , Syscall 175 via insmod" , The container process executes insmod /tmp/net_diag.ko, which invokes sys_finit_module , syscall 313 or sys_init_module , syscall 175 to load the ELF relocatable kernel object directly into host Ring-0 kernel memory while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ insmod /tmp/net_diag.ko / ⇠#2 ACK 313) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 insmod / modprobe Utility), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Shared Host Linux Kernel Ring-0).

keySpecs.value: Enable kernel.modules_disabled=1 via sysctl on immutable Kubernetes worker nodes after boot, enforce CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_FORCE=y (signed kernel modules only), and block init_module/finit_module in the container Seccomp profile.

stages.title: Stage 3: Host Kernel /proc/modules Taint Flag & dmesg Audit Correlation
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1014 - Rootkit)
stages.description: The instant an uncertified foreign gear snaps into the central machinery, the skyscraper master dashboard lights up two unmistakable warning lamps and logs the exact part name in the permanent engine diary for safety inspectors to audit. Loading an unsigned out-of-tree module sets the kernel taint flag (/proc/sys/kernel/tainted bit 12 O = OOT_MODULE and bit 13 E = UNSIGNED_MODULE) and logs a kernel ring-buffer message in dmesg/journald (logged in Linux Audit Event 0 with KernelTaintMask=/proc/sys/kernel/tainted = 12288 , OOT + UNSIGNED, ModuleEntry=/proc/modules -> net_diag, ContainmentAction=Isolate & cordon Kubernetes worker node so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes cat /proc/sys/kernel/tainted && lsmod | head -n 10 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , cat /proc/sys/kernel/tainted && lsmod | head -n 10 via System / Runtime Execution Interface so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1014 during "Host Kernel /proc/modules Taint Flag & dmesg Audit Correlation" , Loading an unsigned out-of-tree module sets the kernel taint flag , /proc/sys/kernel/tainted bit 12 O = OOT_MODULE and bit 13 E = UNSIGNED_MODULE and logs a kernel ring-buffer message in dmesg/journald while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact journalctl -k | grep "loading out-of-tree module taints kernel" runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , journalctl -k | grep "loading out-of-tree module taints kernel" via System / Runtime Executi so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1014 during "Host Kernel /proc/modules Taint Flag & dmesg Audit Correlation" , Loading an unsigned out-of-tree module sets the kernel taint flag , /proc/sys/kernel/tainted bit 12 O = OOT_MODULE and bit 13 E = UNSIGNED_MODULE and logs a kernel ring-buffer message in dmesg/journald while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ kernel: net_diag: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel (tainted=12288) / ⇠#3 ACK 0) from Node ③ (#3 insmod / modprobe Utility) to Node ④ (#4 Syscall 313 (sys_finit_module)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Shared Host Linux Kernel Ring-0).
